candidates.context: This draft guidance is intended to assist applicants preparing to submit to FDA abbreviated new 17 drug applications (ANDAs) and certain prior approval supplements (PASs) to ANDAs. 2 This 18 guidance provides answers to questions we have received from applicants regarding the guidance 19 for industry, ANDA Submissions—Refuse-to-Receive Standards (RTR Standards guidance) 3 and 20 the filing review process, in general. The questions and answers address general issues about the 21 organization of an ANDA, filing decisions made by FDA, the review of and deficiencies related 22 to Drug Master Files (DMFs), product quality, and bioequivalence (BE) and clinical reviews, and 23 are intended to clarify the deficiencies that may cause FDA to refuse to receive (RTR) an 24 ANDA. candidates.statement: FDA will not rescind the RTR determination if a typographical error is the basis for a 214 major deficiency and the applicant informs FDA of the error and provides a corrected 215 submission. When compiling an ANDA, applicants should ensure that all relevant data 216 and information necessary to support the substantive review is correctly transcribed into 217 appropriate sections of the ANDA. When performing a filing review, the Agency will 218 assume that the information transcribed in an ANDA is correct. The Agency must move 219 expeditiously through the filing process to ensure that FDA is able to meet its 220 commitment to review and act on ANDAs within specified GDUFA performance metric 221 goal dates. 222

candidates.statement: In general, an applicant submitting an ANDA for an Rx-to-OTC switch where fewer than 424 all conditions of use were switched to OTC status (“partial Rx-to-OTC switch”) may 425 reference data on the proposed product from an approved ANDA or ANDA that has been 426 received for the prescription drug product that the ANDA applicant also owns instead of 427 conducting new in vivo and in vitro studies to establish BE to the RLD for the OTC 428 product. However, each Rx-to-OTC switch is unique and the requirements for ANDA 429 applicants are based on the characteristics of the OTC RLD including formulation, 430 packaging, conditions of use, among others, and any other requirements specific to OTC 431 products. For example, if the OTC RLD has a different formulation from the Rx RLD, 432 the ANDA applicant will likely need to produce new batches and new BE data. Certain 433 changes in packaging may also result in ANDA applicants needing to produce new 434 batches, with this packaging change also potentially requiring additional data to support 435 BE. An applicant that is referencing an approved ANDA should provide BE summary 436 tables in Module 2.7 in the proposed ANDA. 437

candidates.statement: An applicant using a specific grade of an inactive ingredient should justify the use of that 458 grade, and may not cite to a different grade or a nonspecific listing as support for the 459 safety of the inactive ingredient in the proposed drug product without providing 460 additional justification. Grades of an inactive ingredient may differ in chemical or 461 physical properties and may affect the safety profile of a drug product. Some inactive 462 ingredients have grades or variations that may not have undergone a full safety evaluation 463 in a previously approved product. Some variations may rely, in part, on a finding of 464 safety for an approved drug product that contains a similar grade of the inactive 465 ingredient. The applicant’s justification should identify the differences between the 466 grades of the inactive ingredient and address any implication of the change in grade on 467 the safety of the proposed drug product using a data-driven approach. Whether the safety 468 of a proposed grade of the inactive ingredient, in the context of the currently proposed 469 drug product, is supported by a different grade of the inactive ingredient included in a 470 previously approved drug product will be evaluated during the technical review of the 471 ANDA. 472
